# Core Rule 7 - PvP & Combat
In most scenarios, you should not be shooting or attacking people as soon as you see them. Where and when PvP is allowed depends on the zone you are in — see [textlink="Rule 6 - Zone Rulings" link="RuleC6Stalker"] for the full breakdown. This rule covers how combat should be conducted and what happens when you die.
## Fear Roleplay
All stalkers have their limits, physically and mentally. When playing your character you must recognize immediate or impending danger — you should not constantly put your character in harm's way or ignore it in an unrealistic way. You should not be going out naked with no gear when hunting other players or simply roaming. You know the Zone is dangerous, act like it.
In fights where you are outnumbered or overpowered, such as a 1v2 or when the enemy is significantly more geared than you, you may retreat, hide, or fight back if fired upon. At times this cannot be adequately enforced, however if you have knowledge of your opponent and go against this rule, administrative action will be taken.
Roles like Monolith, Renegades, and Military Stalkers have more leeway on this. Monoliths are brainwashed, feel no pain, and never give up in a fight. Renegades are mentally unstable. Military Stalkers are special forces composed of veteran stalkers or specialized trained military.
## Safe Zone Disengagement
Protections of transitions or within a screen of a green zone do not apply if the encounter started outside of those areas.
You cannot enter any safe zone within 5 minutes of PvP disengagement.
## Escalation
For any faction that is not at [color=#FF0000]war[/color] or in an [color=#008000]alliance[/color] escalation must be followed in [color=##FFFF00]yellow[/color] zones. NOTE: See [textlink="Rule 6 - Zone Rulings" link="RuleC6Stalker"] for how to handle where and when PvP may occur otherwise. On sight PvP is allowed for anyone of the faction of someone you've engaged in PvP with within roughly the last 10 minutes, use good judgement and do not attempt to abuse this to attack uninvolved parties.
[color=##FFA500]Hostile[/color]: For any faction with this relation you may escalate on them for any RP reason following [color=#808080]Gray Zone[/color] rules. Otherwise you may engage in on sight PvP if they pose a clear and immediate danger to a faction member or group member you are travelling with defined below.
[color=##FFFF00]Neutral[/color]: For any faction with this relationship you may escalate on them for a few reasons after an RP exchange of a couple sentences from either side relating to the reasoning. - They are using gear exclusive to your faction without having permission to own it and refuse to return it. - In the case of undercover [textlink="Monolith" link="RuleF4"] they attempt to break your cover; [textlink="Clear Sky" link="RuleF10"] may simply KOS for the same. - They pose a clear and immediate danger to you, someone in your faction, or someone you are travelling with.
Clear and Immediate Danger: To satisfy this condition a few conditions may be filled: - The have someone or the corpse of someone in your faction or traveling group in custody. - There is a credible report of them recently (last 30 minutes) working with someone in a faction at [color=#FF0000]war[/color] with your own for combat operations.
Anyone robbing can be killed on sight by any non-ally non-faction
Anyone can KOS a person wearing Monolith gear (excluding weapons) outside of green and gray zones.
## PvP Death Rules
All rules from dying start from when you leave the latest safe zone (Green Zone, Faction Base). Bodies despawn after 40 minutes, leaving all gear on the ground.
- You can remember where and how you died, but not who killed you or what faction they were from. - You can remember those you started traveling with, but not those you met along the way. - You cannot go back to your dead body until 15 minutes have passed. - Dying to an anomaly or mutant during a PvP fight still counts as a PvP death. - You cannot hint or reveal that you have died in-character to others, or where. - Being revived by a defibrillator still counts as a PvP death
## PvE Death Rules
- You can remember everything up until your death, but not anything after that. - There is no time restriction on going back to your dead body.
Losing your stuff is tough, especially for newer players. If these rules are abused or used in bad faith, freezing in place upon seeing your corpse may be re-implemented.
